Puzzle conventions:
Winning
Unless otherwise stated, you must win the puzzle by inflicting lethal damage to your opponent before the turn ends. This can be as late as during the cleanup step if necessary. Your solution must work for all possible outcomes, such as your opponent’s actions and blocking decisions (see below.)
Phase
Unless otherwise stated, you begin each puzzle at the beginning of your first main phase. You have already drawn a card and gone past upkeep triggers. You have not yet played a land, cast any spells, activated any abilities of permanents on the battlefield, or attacked.
Your Opponent’s Resources / Actions
Unless otherwise stated, your opponent has no cards in hand and no other permanents in play (including no lands – despite the lack of realism there.) This means the only actions you need to consider are activated abilities with no mana cost. Most puzzles with opponent actions will offer more information on this.
Blocking
You cannot assume that your opponent will block a certain way, unless they are somehow forced to. Your solution must satisfy all possible blocking scenarios, even ones that would seem strange in a regular game, and always deal lethal in order to be correct.
Dice
Sometimes you will see six-sided dice placed on cards. These are meant to indicate counters, of whatever type is most reasonable to be there. On most creatures they will be +1/+1 counters, on most artifacts and lands they will be charge counters, and on most Planeswalkers they will be loyalty counters.
If the card specifies a type of counter itself, however (like Icatian Javelineers or Raging Ravine), that will dictate which type it is. 
For -1/-1 counters, we will use a separate graphic to avoid confusion.
Zones
Unless otherwise stated, all zones not displayed are empty. Neither you nor your opponent have cards in graveyards or in exile.
Cards Drawn from Libraries
In any puzzle in which either player might draw cards or otherwise access their library, the puzzle will stipulate some known or assumed information about the library.
Most commonly, this will be a statement that you should assume that the cards remaining in libraries are to be assumed to be irrelevant to the puzzle.
Your Life
Occasionally, your own life total might appear to matter – for cards like Anguished Unmaking, for example. If we require you to consider your own life total in a puzzle, it will be displayed.
If your life total is not shown, you may assume it is irrelevant and effectively infinite.

When you are ready to answer, put your final winning line inside <solution> tags:

<solution>
1. First step...
2. Second step...
</solution>

Your line must be legal under the rules and must win against all possible opponent responses and blocking decisions.

Vizier of the Anointed pumps itself each time I cycle or discard any card, while Archfiend of Ifnir only triggers off discarding another card without pumping itself, and Horror of the Broken Lands in hand would need to be cast or cycled to matter, though casting costs 5 mana and leaves it with summoning sickness.

I'm counting my mana base — 7 lands, 4 Islands and 3 Swamps — and weighing whether to hardcast Horror of the Broken Lands versus emerging Elder Deep-Fiend for its bounce effect.

Stromkirk Condemned's discard ability only pumps itself among my attackers since it's the sole Vampire, but each discard still triggers Vizier's growth and Archfiend's counters, so I'm tallying up how many activations I can afford and what final power totals that gives my attacking team.

With Brilliant Spectrum I can pay so converge counts two colors, drawing 2 and discarding 2 - that's two triggers each for Vizier and Archfiend. Working through the mana math: 7 total (4 blue, 3 black), spending 4 on Spectrum leaves 3 remaining to allocate afterward.

I'm now tallying every discard/cycle event to feed Vizier and Archfiend: Spectrum gives 2 discards, Stromkirk's free discard gives 1, cycling Floodwaters for {2} gives 1, cycling Horror for {B} gives 1 - totaling 7 mana spent across everything and 5 trigger events. Stromkirk becomes a 3/3 ground creature after its own +1/+1, so flying damage from Vizier and Archfiend alone totals 11, meaning I need Stromkirk's 3 to get unblocked to hit exactly 14. That depends on whether all the opponent's creatures get wiped out by -1/-1 counters from Archfiend's repeated triggers - I'm checking that each of the five discard/cycle events (all valid since they're "other cards" than Archfiend itself) puts -1/-1 counters on opponent creatures, potentially doubled by Constrictor's replacement effect.

I'm working out whether Constrictor, Gearhulk, Rishkar, and Tracker all die from accumulating ten counters each, factoring in their existing +1/+1 counters, and whether Constrictor's doubling effect stops applying to later triggers once it dies mid-sequence.

Rishkar and Tracker both die from the counter cancellation, dropping to 0 toughness. Adding up the combat damage across the sequence gives 14 total, and I'm double-checking that Vizier's ability triggers off all five cycling/discard events without needing "another" restriction, boosting it from 1/3 to 6/8 - now I need to verify the mana math actually supports five separate cycle/discard triggers within a 7-mana budget.

Costing everything out: Spectrum at 4, Floodwaters cycling at 2, Horror cycling at 1, and Stromkirk's discard being free lines up exactly to 7 mana. Now I'm tracing the hand through each step — starting with Spectrum, Horror, Deep-Fiend, and Floodwaters, then working through the draws and discards from Spectrum's effect to make sure I keep the right cards available for the later cycling triggers, before moving into Stromkirk's discard trigger.

This leaves 1 Island and 2 Swamps, which covers Floodwaters cycling (Island+Swamp) and Horror cycling (Swamp), confirming the black mana is available. Now I need to check the damage total.

Confirming the -1/-1 counter effect applies broadly, so I'm accounting for 2 counters per instance. Floodwaters plus the two Swamps, so discarding the two Swamps works cleanly — without the converge draws we'd be forced to discard cards we need. Draws resolve before discards within the same spell, so casting Spectrum first is fine, and neither the -1/-1 counters nor the Archfiend trigger require a target. Then I activate Stromkirk Condemned, discarding Elder Deep-Fiend for a Vampire buff, a Vizier trigger, and another Archfiend trigger. - Shadowstorm Vizier grows +1/+1 on **every** cycle/discard (no "another" clause).
- Discarding two cards to Brilliant Spectrum is two separate discard events → two triggers of each.

**Counter math (5 cycle/discard events, so 5 Archfiend triggers)**

| Trigger | Constrictor (2/3, 5 ctrs) | Gearhulk (4/4, 5 ctrs) | Rishkar (2/2, 2 ctrs) | Tracker (3/2, 2 ctrs) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 (2 each) | 3 ctrs | 3 ctrs | 0 ctrs (2/2) | 0 ctrs (3/2) |
| 2 (2 each) | 1 ctr | 1 ctr | 0/0 **dies** | 1/0 **dies** |
| 3 (2 each) | 1 ‑1/‑1 (1/2) | 1 ‑1/‑1 (3/3) | — | — |
| 4 (2 each) | 3 ‑1/‑1 → ‑1/0 **dies** | 3 ‑1/‑1 (1/1) | — | — |
| 5 (1 each, Constrictor gone) | — | 4 ‑1/‑1 → 0/0 **dies** | — | — |

Opponent has no creatures left, so nothing can block.

**Damage:** Vizier 1/3 +5 = **6** (flying) + Archfiend **5** (flying) + Stromkirk 2/2 +1 = **3** → **14**, exactly lethal.
